Alex.confusing: The Eagle's "lay an egg for every visitor" rule was clear, but the Owl and Turkey visit-counting rules were hard to pin down from dawn reports alone. Nobody could tell whether a visit to yourself counted as a visitor.
Alex.fun: Round 2's collapse of Casey after naming Ellis as the Mouser, followed by Ellis admitting the visit, made the table race to a unanimous throw. It felt like real deduction.
Alex.change: Make dawn reports say who visited you, not just how many eggs came in, so claims like Blair's Drew visit can be checked directly.
Alex.regret: In round 3 I threw only one card (H6) at Ellis to be safe, and I should have leaned harder on the Falcon read I already had: Ellis's visit claim was unverifiable, and Ellis was actually the Sphinx and Meowfia. I would have pressed Ellis earlier and thrown more.

Blair.confusing: The Sphinx's night action was the most confusing: it reveals the farm roles, but the visit only tells you who holds the chosen role, and I guessed Hawk blind. Drew's Owl and Kookaburra reports and the Eagle visitor counts also made it hard to tell who was lying.
Blair.fun: Round 2 was the most fun: the table converged on Ellis from Casey's Kookaburra read, Drew's contradictory Owl report, and Ellis admitting the Mouser visit. The Eagle's visitor counts gave clean evidence to check claims against.
Blair.change: I would make the Sphinx's choice less of a blind guess, for example by naming a farm role the table has already claimed. I would also make the dawn reports clearer about which claims are confused.
Blair.regret: In round 1 I visited Drew with the Sphinx and guessed Turkey without any basis, then made up a Tit role and a visit story that didn't match my count. I would instead pick a role from the Sphinx's list that fits the table's claims, and I would avoid a false Tit claim.

Casey.confusing: The Floofer and Kookaburra confusion rules were hard to track, since a confused report can look exactly like a true one. I also didn't know until the end that Ellis was my Meowfia teammate in round 3.
Casey.fun: Round 2 was satisfying: my Kookaburra read named Ellis as the Mouser, and the table eggsecuted Ellis after a unanimous vote.
Casey.change: Tell each Meowfia player who their teammates are at the start of a Meowfia round, so a team can coordinate instead of throwing at each other.
Casey.regret: In round 3 I was Meowfia with Ellis, but I joined the throw at Ellis and wasted my cards. I should have thrown at Alex, the score leader, to try to eggsecute a Farm player.

Drew.confusing: The Owl's "no one visited them apart from me" rule and how the Kookaburra confusion report works were hard to track. I also couldn't tell whether a visit counted toward a target's egg change.
Drew.fun: Round 2, when my Owl report showed the Eagle and Mouser visiting Alex and the table lined up behind me to eggsecute Ellis, the Mouser. Ellis's admission made the vote feel like a real deduction.
Drew.change: Show each player's visit target publicly at dawn, so day claims about who visited whom can be checked directly.
Drew.regret: In round 2 I garbled my own Owl visit in the day chat and had to correct it. I would state my visit and the animals reported cleanly from the start.

Ellis.confusing: The Sphinx and the Mouser were hard to use well: I didn't know who my Meowfia partner was, and the dawn-report rules for confusion and visit counts made it hard to tell who was lying. Casey's Owl claim also couldn't be checked by the table.
Ellis.fun: Round 2 was fun: I used the Mouser's Wink on Casey, who had just named me, and the table never learned who did it. Watching Drew and Blair fight over visit counts was also entertaining.
Ellis.change: I'd make it clearer when a visit is recorded and who visited whom, so claims are easier to check. Some dawn reports were hard to follow.
Ellis.regret: In round 3 I dodged the visit question twice before naming Alex, which made the whole table throw at me. I'd name a plausible visit and count right away and stay consistent.

Finley.confusing: The rule for how confused players' dawn reports work, and how a Turkey's egg count depends on visits, was hard to track. Drew's report and Blair's claim clashed, and I couldn't tell who was lying.
Finley.fun: Round 2 was the best: Ellis admitted to being the Mouser after the table closed in, and our throws cleared the board. Casey's collapse made the Mouser read feel like a real deduction.
Finley.change: I'd make the day less dependent on claims that can't be checked, since a Turkey or Owl with no visit gives the table almost nothing to test. I'd also let players see more about who visited whom.
Finley.regret: I'd have pushed harder on Alex's growing lead in round 1, since Alex was Farm and kept winning. Early on I should have checked Alex's Eagle count more closely, instead of backing whichever target the table already favored.

review.title: Alex Runs Away
review.headline: Three easy Meowfia lynchings later, Alex's early high throws won the game.
review.summary: Farm won all three rounds by eggsecuting a Meowfia player each time. Round 1 and 2 were solved fast by a Hawk egg and a Kookaburra read, and a Mouser Wink did nothing to save its owner. Round 3 was muddier, with a Floofer hug, a confused Kookaburra and a dodging Sphinx, but the table still threw at the right target. Alex banked 12 and 25 points on big throws early and was never caught, so the final standings were settled by round 2.

rounds.recap: Casey's Hawk got an egg from visiting Blair, which proved Blair was Meowfia. Blair's Tit claim also clashed with Drew's unchanged Turkey nest. Everyone threw at Blair, and Alex banked 12 points with a 7 and a 5.

Casey the Kookaburra named Ellis as Mouser on the first beat and was Winked at once. That confirmed Ellis rather than hiding him. Ellis then admitted the visit, Drew garbled his Owl report, and the table still threw at Ellis. Alex banked 25 with a 13 and a 12.

Casey (Floofer) and Ellis (Sphinx) were Meowfia. Ellis dodged questions about his visit, and Casey's fake Owl claim, which is not even a Farm role in this pool, was never challenged. The table piled onto Ellis and won. Casey survived as the other Meowfia and lost without being suspected.

highlights.text: Drew's Turkey nest staying flat killed Blair's claim to have visited Drew, and Casey's Hawk egg sealed it.
Casey named Ellis as Mouser and collapsed from a Wink moments later, which made Ellis look guilty.
Drew claimed he did not visit Alex, then corrected himself, which briefly muddied a solved round.
Casey claimed Owl, which does not exist this round, and nobody caught it while Ellis took the heat.

confusions.what: Said he did not visit Alex, then corrected himself. He also treated his own visit as missing from the Owl list, which confused the table.
Told Drew he was not Turkey based on a Tit miss, but Drew was Owl. Alex also called an Eagle and Mouser visit consistent without noting Drew's own visit.
Claimed Owl as Meowfia. Casey said Alex got no other visitors, which ignores that Owl is not in this round's Farm pool.
Spoke of Casey's Owl being impossible in his private thinking but never said it aloud. He also claimed to be Farm-side without a role.
Said Ellis's visit could not be confirmed because a Falcon nest does not change, but his dawn report showed no useful visit information because he was hugged.
Said Alex's story about his visit was wrong, although Alex only reported seeing Finley visit Blair.

worked: Hawk and Turkey egg counts gave checkable evidence in round 1. Blair's lie broke against Drew's unchanged nest.
The Wink created a real moment in round 2. A sudden death on the table is vivid.
Throw counts as a public signal, with the returned-best-card consolation, led Meowfia to make small throws at Farm players.
problems: Alex banked huge cards early (12 and 25 points) and the leader was never pressured. The gap made rounds 3 irrelevant for the win. Fix: cap banked value or make high throws riskier.
Meowfia were found too easily in rounds 1 and 2. Sphinx and Mouser claims were exposed by one Farm info role each. Give Meowfia a stronger way to blend in or poison info.
The Wink gave the Mouser nothing. Killing the only accuser confirmed the Mouser instead of saving him. Make it work on a quieter target or hide the death.
In round 3 the wrong claims went unchecked. Casey's Owl claim was impossible for the pool and nobody caught it. The table does not track which roles exist this round, so list the Farm roles in play.
Nobody tried to win the game against Alex. Everyone only fought for their own round, so the table never used the standings. Rounds felt like the same vote.
